articleTitle: The public as end user (library uses of CD-ROMS)
abstract: The traditional relationship of the library and the scholar remains. The individual retains a freedom of choice of a wide range of source materials. The library acquires a balanced range, and offers training and advice on its use. The author looks at how CD-ROMs are being used in Sutton Central Library.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: CDROM in the domestic UK market
abstract: Discusses the main reasons that CD-ROM has failed to take off in the UK. They include price and lack of useful software.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Towards hypermedia: technical issues become passee
abstract: The author looks at the history of hypermedia together with current developments. The author states that the issues on which the success of hypermedia depends are classification, indexing and retrieval.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Hardware and software in a nontechnical environment
abstract: At present CD-ROMs are almost entirely limited to the business, professional and educational worlds. The technology has not penetrated into the domestic market to a significant extent although optical discs are often thought to have enormous potential in this sector. There are a number of reasons why CD has made little impact of which the most obvious are the high cost of the equipment, and the nature of the products currently available. As hardware and disc costs fall these barriers will no doubt be lowered and other considerations will become important. The paper focuses on one of these other considerations; namely the technical problems currently faced by users of optical disc systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
